Bacha Coffee is the standout: a huge Moroccan-style space with 200+ Arabica coffees, though it's takeaway only, so you'd sip it as you walk or by your gate. results.message: Since you're in T1, the Snooze Lounge is your best bet: free reclining chairs with dimmed lighting, a quiet zone and little privacy screens, no booking needed (first-come, first-served). If you'd prefer something more restful and private, the Ambassador Transit Hotel is a great use of a long layover, and with about 4 hours to boarding you've got time to unwind at its rooftop pool, though I'd keep an eye on the clock so you're at your gate with a buffer.

results.message: For proper local food in T2, T2 Food Gallery is the best-value pick: hawker-style stalls for Hainanese chicken rice, laksa and nasi lemak all under one roof. Heavenly Wang is a quick, authentic kopitiam option for Singapore kopi, teh and kaya toast, or a nasi lemak set. Both are landside, outside immigration, so they suit you best if you haven't cleared immigration yet. If you're already airside, Old Chang Kee's curry puffs are the fastest local snack, and the nasi lemak at dnata Lounge is genuinely good if you have a long wait.

results.message:
Good news: you're in T4 with plenty of time, so you can browse at an easy pace. Taste Singapore is the best one-stop for edible souvenirs like laksa paste, chilli crab sauce and kaya jam, and Zakkasg is great for cute, budget-friendly small gifts. If you want something truly exclusive, the Lego Airport Store has Changi-themed sets you can't get elsewhere (allow about 20 minutes if you try the Build a Minifigure station).

Here's a simple walking order with your 105 usable minutes:
1. Heritage Zone (~15 min): a free, interactive Peranakan heritage display, a nice way to start and get some inspiration.
2. TWG Tea Salon (~20 min): the 1837 Black Tea is the signature, and their tea also makes a classy gift.
3. Lego Airport Store (~10-20 min): look for the exclusive Changi Airport set.
4. Taste Singapore and Zakkasg: fill in the rest of your time with food souvenirs and small gifts.

That leaves you comfortably ahead of the 15-minute gate buffer, but do keep an eye on the clock as queues can vary.
